research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10319 (17 FR 188, Federal Register of January 8, 1952; the govinfo PDF text layer), headed Executive Order 10319, signed by Harry S. Truman and dated January 4, 1952; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier listed seventeen clauses, but sixteen of them are fee-schedule paragraphs (spirits of turpentine, rosin, drums, tank cars) of a Department of Agriculture naval-stores rule printed on the same Federal Register page after the order. I replace them with one whole-order clause running from the heading to the sentence ending "dispute arose." The order has three recitals and four operative sentences: the creation of a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act with the rule that no member be interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; the direction to report within thirty days from the date of the order; the direction that the board comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 of the Railway Labor Act. The order does not mention any other Executive order or any officer other than the President. Later facts: the National Mediation Board's held record for Emergency Board No. 100 (PEB-100-Report.pdf) states that the board members were never named because the parties returned to direct negotiations, that the President granted three thirty-day extensions of time, that the parties reached an agreement dated April 24, 1952, and that no report to the President was made. The agreement date is recorded here as a spent fact and the order is disclosed as functionally spent on 1952-04-24; The record is held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10319_Report_of_the_emergency_board_created_by_EO_10319_of_January_4_1952_Northwest_Airline_121b7de808.txt; it is pinned here by path and quotation because the claim kit's working-text gate treats a report file registered under this order's number as a copy of the order itself and refuses it as an event or note source while the official order text is held.  the board was never constituted (owner rulings of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines and on a board never constituted). Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553 naming this order. The held-text number-citation scan in the packet lookups found no other held text citing 10319.
savings_reason: EO 12553 attaches no savings or exception clause to its revocation list (its enacting provision is one sentence followed by the table). The board was never constituted and made no report; the dispute was settled by the parties' own agreement of April 24, 1952, which is not a command of this order. No continuing right or duty arising from the order is shown.
earlier_end_check: Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline and not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines); here no report was ever made, according to the National Mediation Board record. (2) The three thirty-day extensions of reporting time named in that record extended the deadline only; their dates and instruments are not held, and an extension is not an end. (3) The status-quo period runs, by the order's own words, until thirty days after the board reports; no report was made, and the dispute was settled by agreement on April 24, 1952, so the order was functionally spent on that date but stayed on the books (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on a board never constituted: treat it like the other emergency-board orders until express revocation). (4) The section 502 compliance sentence is a condition on how the board performs its functions; the Defense Production Act is not held in this packet and no expiry of it is claimed as an end. (5) The OFR catalog and the number-citation scan show no instrument other than EO 12553 that revokes, supersedes or amends this order. No earlier end is shown.
scope_check: EO 12553 revokes the order by number with no exception and reaches any amendments, so the single whole-order clause ends in full on that date. No amendment of the order is held.
independent_command_check: The order has no command independent of the board: the report direction and the section 502 compliance direction concern the board's work, and the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute and which ran only until thirty days after a report. The order creates no office, fund, delegation or right that outlived the board.

research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10634 (20 FR 6433, Federal Register of September 1, 1955), signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower and dated August 25, 1955; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: one whole-order clause. Under the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, the order provides that, whenever financial assistance is not otherwise available on reasonable terms, loans (including participations in, or guarantees of, loans) under section 302 of that Act may be made to aid the reconstruction, rehabilitation or replacement of facilities destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, whenever the facilities are required for national defense as determined by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization. Later events (strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21, each recorded with date, actor, mechanism and before and after text): EO 10773 (effective July 1, 1958) amends every reference in prior orders to the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization to refer to the Director of the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization; EO 11051 section 601 (1962-09-27) amends the references in this order to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization and its Director to refer to the Office of Emergency Planning and its Director; EO 11725 section 3 (effective July 1, 1973) transfers the authority then vested in the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness under this order to the Administrator of General Services. None of them revokes or terminates the order. Ending: EO 12148 section 5-106 revokes the order, effective July 15, 1979 by that order's own effective-date sentence (signed July 20, 1979). Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code search has two hits, a note under 42 U.S.C. 5195 reprinting EO 12148 with its section 5-106 revocation and the title 50 disposition table listing this order as omitted; the eCFR search has two hits for which the dossier holds no located text, so they were not relied on either way; the Federal Register catalog notes (five machine hits) record the amendments by EO 10773 and EO 11051, a cross-reference to EO 11725 and the revocation by EO 12148.
savings_reason: EO 12148 attaches no savings sentence to the section 5-106 revocation, and the held text contains no general savings clause (searched for saving, remain in, continue in, nothing in and notwithstanding). Loans already made would be governed by their own terms and by section 302 of the Defense Production Act, not by this order; no continuing right or duty arising only from the order is shown.
earlier_end_check: Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The order has no sunset or condition ending it. (2) EO 10773, EO 11051 and EO 11725 change which officer makes the national-defense determination or holds the authority; each is recorded as a later event, and none revokes or terminates the order. (3) The intervening statutory renamings of the mobilization office (from the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization, and from the Office of Emergency Planning to the Office of Emergency Preparedness) are not shown by any held source and do not name the order, so they are not recorded as events or ends. (4) No held source shows that the section 302 loan authority lapsed before 1979; that possibility is not excluded, but it is not supported by held evidence, and the order is permissive, so it is not treated as ended by disuse. (5) EO 12148 names the order and revokes it, effective July 15, 1979.
scope_check: One clause covers the whole order. EO 12148 section 5-106 revokes the order, as amended, without exception, so the whole order ends on that date.
independent_command_check: The loan authority itself is conferred by section 302 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, which the order invokes and which is not held in this packet. The order adds only the permission to use that authority for major-disaster facilities that the named officer determines are required for national defense; it creates no separate continuing command.
savings_check: No savings wording in EO 12148 attaches to the revocation; loans already made are past transactions governed by their own terms and the statute.

research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10915 (26 FR 781, Federal Register of January 26, 1961), signed by John F. Kennedy and dated January 24, 1961; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: I confirm the dossier's three scopes: (1) the recitals and section 1, which amends EO 10900 by renumbering its sections 6 and 7 as 7 and 8 and inserting a new section 6 (Director of the Food-for-Peace Program); (2) section 2, the command amending EO 10893 by adding a new section 111 at the end of its Part I; (3) the text of section 111 itself. Ends: section 2 and section 111 end on 1961-09-30, when EO 10973 section 605(b) supersedes section 2 of EO 10915 by name and section 605(a) supersedes EO 10893 except Part II and one funding purpose (section 607 makes EO 10973 effective as of September 30, 1961). The inserted section 6 of EO 10900 ends on 1980-06-27, when EO 12220 section 1-501 revokes EO 10900 as amended. Later events on the inserted section 6: EO 11252 (effective 1965-11-01) transfers all functions of the Director of the Food-for-Peace Program, including those under EO 10900 as amended, to the Secretary of State and modifies that order accordingly; EO 11963 section 2 (1977-01-19) revokes section 5 of EO 10900 and redesignates sections 6, 7 and 8 as sections 5, 6 and 7, so the inserted Food-for-Peace section became section 5. The whole-order end is the latest clause end, 1980-06-27. The dossier's missing items were resolved by reading the held texts: EO 10924 section 4 says it does not supersede or derogate from EO 10893; EO 11963 was read in full, and EO 12148 and EO 12220 were searched for every provision naming EO 10900. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog notes (four machine hits) record the partial supersession by EO 10973 and notes naming EO 11963 and EO 12148 as amending.
savings_reason: Section 606 of EO 10973 ("Saving provisions.") continues determinations, orders and other actions taken with respect to any function affected by that order, and not revoked or made inapplicable before its date, until amended, modified or terminated by appropriate authority. Actions taken under section 111 are therefore accrued effects; they do not keep section 111 operative. The functions of the Director under section 6 of EO 10900 were transferred to the Secretary of State by EO 11252; EO 12220 has no savings clause of its own.
earlier_end_check: Section 2 and section 111: the first end is the supersession by name in EO 10973 section 605(b), with section 605(a) superseding EO 10893 except Part II and except for the purposes of using funds under section 643(c) of the Act; section 111 sat in Part I and served the coordination of section 402 functions, not that funding purpose, and section 605(b) supersedes section 2 of EO 10915 without exception. EO 10924 section 4 states that it does not supersede EO 10893 and is not an event. EO 12163 (effective October 1, 1979) later revoked what remained of EO 10893, after the 1961 end, so it does not change these dates. Section 1 and the inserted section 6: EO 11252 transferred the Director's functions to the Secretary of State and modified EO 10900 accordingly, without naming EO 10915 or printing replacement text; EO 11963 section 2 later redesignated the same section as section 5, which shows that the section was still part of EO 10900 in 1977, so EO 11252 is recorded as a later event and not as an end. The other amendments of EO 10900 in the held corpus change other parts of that order and leave the inserted section unchanged: EO 10972 (section 4(d)), EO 11036 (sections 4(a), 4(d)(5) and 4(d)(7)), EO 11051 section 601 (references to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization), EO 11963 section 1 (a new subsection (d) of section 1), EO 12148 section 5-107 (revocation of section 4(d)(2)) and EO 12163 section 1-903(b)(4) (a new subsection of section 3). The first end of the inserted section is EO 12220 section 1-501.
scope_check: Three scopes, each decided separately: section 2 and section 111 end on 1961-09-30; the recitals are not operative; section 1 is an executed amendment whose inserted section 6 (later section 5) of EO 10900 ends with that order on 1980-06-27. The whole-order end is the latest clause end, 1980-06-27.
independent_command_check: Each amendatory command was performed on issue; what survived was the inserted text, which ended with the superseded or revoked parent text. Section 6 of EO 10900 and section 111 of EO 10893 describe the same Director's coordinating role in two different parent orders and end on different dates; no independent standing command remains.

research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11036 (27 FR 6653, Federal Register of July 13, 1962), signed by John F. Inventory: the dossier splits the order into two contiguous clauses at an OCR break inside the substituted section 4(a)(1) (the second clause begins with a sentence fragment labelled Section 104). Ending: EO 12220 section 1-501 revokes EO 10900 as amended on 1980-06-27. The cited source is the held Federal Register text of EO 12220; the dossier's located-provision record for this pair is an American Presidency Project transcription and is not cited. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the note on this order recording its revocation by EO 12220 and the note recording this order's amendment of EO 10900. EO 12220 cites paragraphs (f) and (j) where this order cited 104(g) and 104(s); whether those are the same statutory paragraphs relettered is not shown by a held statute and is not relied on. EO 12220 has no express savings clause, and no U.S. Code, eCFR or catalog hit shows any other continuing effect of this order.

research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11138 (29 FR 225, Federal Register of January 9, 1964), signed by Lyndon B. Johnson and dated January 7, 1964; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers every operative sentence; I confirm it. The order modifies Executive Order 9721 of May 10, 1946, as amended by Executive Order 10103 of February 1, 1950 (transfer of personnel to public international organizations): it waives, for one named person, Frederick Strauss, the section 1 limit on the period during which a transferred employee is considered on leave of absence and the section 3(a) limit on the time within which reemployment rights may be exercised, and provides that he shall be considered to have been on leave of absence from August 12, 1957 through September 16, 1962 for the purpose of all rights and benefits provided by EO 9721, as amended. Parent order: Executive Order 10804 of February 12, 1959 (24 FR 1147, held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10804.txt), section 2, revoked EO 9721 and EO 10103, except that "each shall be considered to" remain in effect for any employee subject to it who was serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act and did not elect coverage under that Act, and for rights and benefits vested before that date. EO 11138 was issued after that revocation and modifies EO 9721 only for one employee whose deemed leave began on August 12, 1957, before the 1958 Act; the President thus treated EO 9721 as still applying to him within the saved scope. The held evidence does not show the enactment date of the Act (EO 10804 cites it as 72 Stat. 961) or whether Mr. Strauss elected coverage under it; if he had, the saved parent would not have applied to him and the waiver would have had no field of operation. That question bears on the waiver's effect, not on whether this order stayed on the books, and EO 10804, being earlier, cannot be an end of this 1964 order. EO 12553 revoked EO 9721, EO 10103 and this order on the same day. Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553 naming this order.
savings_reason: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception attached to its revocation list. The deemed leave of absence for August 12, 1957 through September 16, 1962 and any rights that vested in the named person under it before the revocation are accrued consequences, not a continuing command of this order.
earlier_end_check: No held source shows a revocation, supersession or expiry of this order before EO 12553; its own text has no end date or condition, and the waiver covers a past period and two time limits rather than a future event. Whether the waiver was used, and so exhausted by performance, is not established by held evidence: no held source shows whether or when Mr. Strauss exercised reemployment rights or claimed benefits under it (owner ruling 2026-10-28: an unestablished event is not claimed as an interval). The 1959 revocation of the parent orders by EO 10804, with its saving for employees serving on the enactment date of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act and for vested rights, came before this order and cannot end it; this order operated, as the President framed it, within that saved scope. The first end shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25.
scope_check: Single clause, whole order, one named person. EO 12553 revokes the whole order by its own row, and also revokes the parent orders EO 9721 and EO 10103 on the same day.
independent_command_check: The order's only command is the waiver and deeming rule for the named person; there is no independent continuing command. The parent EO 9721 did not continue generally after 1959: EO 10804 section 2 revoked it and EO 10103, keeping them in effect only for employees serving with an international organization on the enactment date of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act who did not elect coverage under it, and for rights vested before that date; EO 12553 then revoked both parents in 1986.
savings_check: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception. The deemed leave status for 1957-1962 is an accrued consequence; no held source shows a later right or duty depending on this order after 1986-02-25.

savings_check: No savings language in EO 12060; the placement of the positions is carried by the statute, and earlier pay is accrued.
